doc.title: Eiji Kitamura interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: 1972 trip to Toronto with Teddy Wilson and Gene Krupa
summary: In 1972 he played in Toronto with Wilson, met Krupa, and heard the Greatest Jazz Band at Massey Hall.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Oh I’ve never been there. Because once Teddy Wilson, he played [inaudible] jazz clubs, a very small club, and I went only once. And after I went to Toronto, Teddy and Al Bruno the bassist and me, and then I met Gene Krupa and Teddy Wilson and I played the clarinet. I am very excited. And then after, I went to Syracuse and Buffalo.
That’s right where we come from, near there. What year was that do you recall?
1972. And then I went to the Massey Hall in Toronto, and I heard the greatest jazz band, with Yank Lawson and Bobby Hackett and Bob Wilber. I didn’t know Bob Wilber, but he is a marvelous player.

He sure is. Do you know Massey Hall is where they made a recording of what they called “The Greatest Jazz Concert Ever” with Charlie Parker and Dizzy and Bud Powell and — who else was on it — I’m trying to remember, but that was quite a famous record. I think Max Roach was on it too. So you were on the same stage all those fellows too.
And I heard The Greatest Jazz Band. And it was so nice. Only my mouth is open. So surprised.
